clinician.final_diagnosis: Lead perforation following pacemaker implantation, leading to iatrogenic intercostal artery perforation, a large hemothorax and life-threatening hemorrhagic shock
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 80-year-old woman underwent dual chamber pacemaker implantation with active fixation leads for bradycardia-tachycardia syndrome at a regional hospital. On the night following implantation, she developed acute chest pain. Two days post-implantation, she presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain, rapid atrial fibrillation, hypertension (197/109 mm Hg), and decreased left-sided breath sounds. Initial labs showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 130 g/L), elevated troponin T (33 ng/L), and mildly elevated CRP (9 mg/L). Contrast-enhanced CT thorax identified a large left-sided hemothorax and right ventricular lead perforation. By ICU day 1, hemoglobin had declined to 76 g/L (54 g/L drop), indicating massive acute hemorrhage consistent with life-threatening hemorrhagic shock. A left-sided thoracotomy tube was inserted, draining 1.5 L of dark blood. Surgical exploration identified the bleeding source in the lateral intercostal space, which was sealed using sutures and reinforced with a topical fibrin sealant patch. During surgery, the patient received 7 units of erythrocytes and 7 units of plasma. Postoperatively, hemoglobin levels stabilized, and no additional blood transfusions were necessary.
